assumptions: Each Group in the Cq table is one condition with enough samples for geNorm to rank on its own.
Cq values are on a common scale across conditions.
limits: geNorm cannot order its two most stable genes, so they share a rank.
Agreement between conditions is not stability within any one of them.
bio.jane/contract.question: Does a reference-gene stability ranking hold across conditions, and which candidates rank well everywhere?

description: Ask whether a reference-gene stability ranking holds across conditions, and which candidate genes rank well everywhere rather than in one tissue or treatment. Each condition (the Group column of a long-format Cq table) is ranked by geNorm on its own samples; the conditions are then the blocks of a Friedman test and Kendall's W says how far they agree (0 independent orders, 1 the same order everywhere), with an asymptotic χ² p and a Monte Carlo p from shuffling each condition's ranks. Returns every gene's rank in every condition, its mean rank (the meta-ranking) and its best and worst. geNorm cannot order its two most stable genes, so they share rank 1.5 in every condition. Use `rank_reference_genes` for one condition's ranking by all four algorithms.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

cq_table.description: the long-format table `Target,Sample,Group,Cq`, one row per measurement; Group is the condition each sample was measured in, and every gene must be measured in every sample.

permutations.description: shuffles of the ranks within each condition. The smallest p is 1 / (permutations + 1).

seed.description: seed for the shuffles. Each permutation draws from its own stream, so one can be re-run alone. Advanced.

name: discover_reference_concordance

conditions.description: each condition's geNorm order with M

genes.description: every gene, most stable on average first: its rank in each condition, mean rank, best and worst

nullModel.description: the null, stated with every run

p.description: Monte Carlo p of W against within-condition shuffles

w.description: Kendall's coefficient of concordance across conditions
